$schema_note: Language-neutral runtime validation rules for InfinityForge Tracking adapters. Companion to malformed-payload-rules.md, which is authoritative for prose explanation; this file exists for adapters/tests to reference a rule by stable id. Every rule is derived from an existing file under specification/ or schema/ — see 'source' on each rule.

action_vocabulary.reject_call: The whole API call (identify/screen) is a no-op; nothing is recorded.
action_vocabulary.drop_event: The entire event is not emitted.
action_vocabulary.drop_metric: The entire metric is not emitted.
action_vocabulary.drop_field: Only the offending property/dimension/field is removed; the rest of the event/metric is still emitted if it remains valid.
action_vocabulary.correct_field: The offending value is deterministically corrected in place and the event/metric is still emitted.
action_vocabulary.not_malformed: This is explicitly allowed by the contract; no correction, drop, or error occurs.

rules.trigger: A field required by schema/event-envelope.yaml or schema/metric-envelope.yaml is absent, null, or an empty string.
A present envelope field does not match its documented type/pattern in schema/common-types.yaml.
Any field, property, or dimension value is null.
A canonical event's property marked required: true is absent.
A canonical property's supplied value does not match its declared type. A stringified boolean ("true"/"false") or 0/1 in place of a boolean is a type mismatch.
A canonical enum-typed property's value is not among its documented allowed_values.
rules.note: Governs emission only. Consuming systems must treat an unrecognized enum value permissively — that is a separate, non-runtime-validation rule.

rules.trigger: An event with a paired price/currency property pair (currently subscription_started, purchase_completed) has exactly one of the pair present.
A property key equals a reserved envelope field name (event, schema_version, timestamp, app_id, environment, platform, sdk_version, sdk_name, app_version, user_id, anonymous_id, properties).
The event name or a property key does not match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*[a-z0-9]$ (min length 2).
The event name does not match any entry in events/*.yaml.
rules.note: App-specific events are explicitly permitted. Still subject to every other rule in this file.

rules.trigger: screen() is called with an empty or missing screen name.
A canonical metric's dimension marked required: true is absent.
value is absent, not a number, or negative.
rules.note: Never coerce a negative value to its absolute value — drop instead, since that would silently change meaning.

rules.trigger: unit is absent or not one of currency|count|impression|millisecond|second|other.
unit is currency and currency is absent, OR unit is not currency and currency is present.
A canonical dimension's value does not match its declared type (string|integer|boolean|enum), or an enum dimension's value is not among allowed_values.
A dimension key collides with a reserved metric-envelope field name, or is not snake_case.
source is absent or not one of application|billing_system|advertising_system|operating_system|network|provider|other.
A canonical metric with a declared fixed_value (currently ad_impression, handled_error; both fixed at 1) is recorded with a different value.
rules.note: This is the one rule in this document where correction is chosen over dropping. errors.md/metrics.md's "correct what can be unambiguously corrected, or drop... or queue... in that order of preference" leaves room for either choice per rule; a fixed_value declaration makes the correct value genuinely unambiguous (exactly one possible right answer), unlike e.g. event.non_snake_case_identifier's case transliteration, which is a guess about intent and so drops instead.

rules.trigger: schema_version is absent or not a positive integer.
metric_name does not match any entry in metrics/*.yaml.
rules.note: App-specific metrics are explicitly permitted. Still subject to every other rule in this file.

rules.trigger: identify() is called with an empty string or no argument.
identify(new_user_id) is called with a different user_id than the one already active, without an intervening reset().
rules.note: Contract explicitly leaves the specific defensive behavior undefined; must never crash. Correctness burden is on the calling application to sequence reset() then identify().
